instruction: My partner has asked me for cable bills over email for tax purposes. Compile all cable bills I have ever received over Gmail into a "bills_cable.zip" and send it to their with a note, "Please see attached.", as a reply to that email. The files in zip should be named "MM-YYYY.pdf" as per the month it is the bill for.
notes: Apps: supervisor, gmail, file_system. The partner is identified as the sender of the inbox email asking for cable bills (no phone lookup needed); the reply goes to that email so recipients default to the partner and no new thread is created. The number of cable bill emails is unknown up front; the problem instantiates three placeholder bill threads/attachments/pdf files (the real count is discovered at runtime from gmail.show_inbox_threads and the download step is repeated once per bill). Completeness of the zip is enforced structurally without quantifiers: bill files form a download chain starting at the bills directory (next-bill-file), compress_directory requires the last file of the chain to exist, and reply requires the zip to be built, so every bill is downloaded (directly as ~/bills_cable/MM-YYYY.pdf via download_to_file_path) before compression. create_directory is done first so the download target directory exists; compress_directory keeps delete_directory at its default (no files removed, only the pdfs and the zip are added, which the evaluation allows). One inbox search with query "cable bill" is assumed to surface both the partner's request thread and the bill threads; show_thread is used to obtain email ids and attachment ids. supervisor-complete-task carries the goal records (request email, body, zip) as non-API parameters and no answer.
